land.text: Sharwan, listed under Arran in the Abbasid province of Arminiya and governed by the Yazidid Shaybanis (Yazid ibn Mazyad d. 801; Khalid and Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Yazid as ostikans of Arminiya)

predecessors.note: The Shirvanshah page: 'The first Yazidi to use the title of Shirvanshah was Yazid's grandson Haytham ibn Khalid in 861'.

land.text: Shirvan as a Safavid province 'governed by appointed officials' after Tahmasp I removed the Shirvanshahs in 1538

successors.note: Ismail I had toppled the dynasty in December 1500 and let the family rule for some more years under Safavid suzerainty.

capitals.name: Shamakhi (Yazidiya)
capitals.note: The page names Shamakhi, also called Yazidiya, as the early seat; Qubad fortified it in 1045.

capitals.name: Baku
capitals.note: 'Baku as the residence from the time of Akhsitan I' after Qizil Arslan seized Shamakhi (reign 1186-1191); approximate: Ibrahim I died at Shamakhi in 1417 and Jabani (1500) lies near it, so the court used both.

correction.text: no Shirvanshah state before 861: for 825-839 use nothing; the state's own first years are new keyframe shirvan_861 on the 866 shape

keyframe_review.note: 113,084 km2 (bbox 43.6-50.3E, 38.5-42.0N), 2.7 times the 41,531 km2 of the 866 shape and reaching into Armenia: not the Shirvanshah state. Its first ruler to use the title was Haytham ibn Khalid in 861; before that Sharwan was only a unit under Arran in the Abbasid province of Arminiya (the Arminiya page: Arran, Bab al-Abwab and Sharwan 'treated as separate units' in the first half of the 9th century; ostikans Khalid ibn Yazid 813 and 828-832, Muhammad ibn Khalid c. 842/844-?). The Shirvan page's 'from 809' for the dynasty is not corroborated. Draw nothing for the Shirvanshahs in 825-860.

New keyframe for 861-865, which Cliopatria lacks (its first usable shape is 866): the 866 shape carried back to Haytham ibn Khalid's title of 861. The pages give no boundary; the 866 shape is a reading of Shirvan, Baku and Shamakhi.

41,531 km2 (bbox 45.8-50.3E, 39.3-41.8N): Shirvan with Baku, Shamakhi and the Absheron peninsula and, in the west, the Kura plain toward Ganja. The Shirvanshah page names Shirvan, Darband, Baku, Shamakhi, Shabaran, Layzan, Khursan, Quba, Maskat, Arran, Muqan, Shakki, Qabala, Baylaqan but gives no area and no boundary; accepted at the era's precision, west edge soft.
41,554 km2 (+0.1 percent): noise; the page has no event in 886 (Cliopatria's Bagratid Armenia starts that year to the west).
41,940 km2 (+0.9 percent): noise; the page has no land change in 947, only Rus in 1030 and Hudud al-'Alam's domain 'that now includes Layzan and Khursan' in 982.
41,891 km2: unchanged. 982: the Hudud al-'Alam describes a domain including Layzan and Khursan; 991-1027 Yazid ibn Ahmad has a complete run of coinage.
41,964 km2: unchanged. 1030: 'Manuchihr I was defeated near Baku by invading Rus', who sacked Baylaqan; no land passes.
41,818 km2 (-0.3 percent): noise; Qubad fortified Shamakhi in 1045 and 1063 saw a Shaddadid siege of Shamakhi, neither a change of land.

42,231 km2 (+1.0 percent): noise. In 1066/67 Qarategin's Seljuks twice ravaged 'the areas of Baku and Maskat' and Fariburz I paid 70,000 dinars of tribute, later 40,000: a suzerainty, not an annexation.
41,867 km2: unchanged to 1084. Cliopatria draws nothing for Shirvan in 1085-1125; Fariburz I reigned 1063-1096 and the dynasty continued, so see new keyframe shirvan_1085.

correction.text: the 1072 shape carried through the gap 1085-1123, as a Seljuk tributary

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1085-1123, a gap in Cliopatria: the 1072 shape carried forward. The page has Fariburz I (1063-1096) paying Seljuk tribute, a dynastic dispute after his death in 1094, and Manuchihr III from 1120 (placed by David IV); the Seljuk invasion under Mahmud II is 1118-1131.

correction.text: eastern Shirvan (Shamakhi, Baku, Quba) without the western piece annexed by Georgia in 1124

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1124-1125: after David IV's September 1124 campaign David IV 'annexed the western Shirvan, handing its government over to Mtsignobartukhutsesi Simon' and 'left the eastern Shirvan to his son-in-law, Manuchihr III as a Georgian protectorate' [quote corrected to the page wording, reviewer eu-19-c]. Cliopatria's 1126 piece (5,687 km2, 46.8-48.1E) is the western part, so eastern Shirvan is the 1139 shape without it.

correction.text: eastern Shirvan (Shamakhi, Baku, Quba) without the western piece annexed by Georgia in 1124

keyframe_review.note: 5,687 km2: this piece lies west of Shamakhi (lon 46.8-48.1E), which is the part the page gives to Georgia in 1124, not the Shirvanshah core; the Shirvanshahs kept eastern Shirvan as a Georgian protectorate until 'Demetrius restored the Shirvanshahs to power in Shirvan' in 'probably 1129 or 1130'. The shape is replaced for 1126-1129 by eastern Shirvan; for 1130 on see shirvan_1130.

correction.text: all Shirvan, restored to the Shirvanshahs

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1130-1138: 'This probably happened in 1129 or 1130, when Demetrius restored the Shirvanshahs to power in Shirvan'; Cliopatria draws the full 42,037 km2 shape again from 1139.

42,037 km2, valid for 1139-1200. 'At the start of the 13th century, the Shirvanshahs conquered Darband, seemingly putting an end to its ruling dynasty' [quote corrected to the page wording, reviewer eu-19-c]; Derbent (42.06N) lies north of the shape's edge (41.78N), so from 1201 use shirvan_1201. 12th century: Seljuk vassals until Toghrul III (1176-1194); Georgian interference in the early 1190s made Shirvan a tributary of Georgia (Georgian-Seljuk wars page).

New keyframe for 1201-1226: the 1139 shape plus Derbent, conquered by the Shirvanshahs at 'the start of the 13th century'. Whether Derbent stayed Shirvanshah to 1235 is not on the page; Ibrahim I 'recovered the borders ... as far as Derbent in north' later (Ibrahim I page).

42,231 km2 (+0.5 percent), 1227-1235, with Derbent added as in shirvan_1201. 1225: 'Shirvanshah Garshasp I (r. after 1203 - 1233/34) was ordered by the Khwarazmshah' to pay tribute. The Mongol campaign against Georgia and Armenia of 1236 (Mongol invasions of Georgia page, silent on Shirvan) follows this shape.

correction.text: the 1227 shape carried through the Mongol gap, as a Mongol suzerainty (soft)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1236-1343, a gap in Cliopatria: the 1227 shape carried forward at confidence 1. The Shirvanshah page: 'The Mongol Empire holds suzerainty' 1206-1368, Ilkhanate suzerainty 1256-1335 with no Shirvan coins known, then Jalayirid suzerainty from 1335; the dynasty is not recorded as interrupted. The Mongol page dates 'in 1236, a large army against Georgia and its vassal Armenian princedoms' and the Ilkhanid placement of Georgia in 1256 but names Shirvan only in an undated 1221 raid.

44,163 km2 (+4.6 percent on 1227): Shirvan under the Jalayirid sultans (page: 'Shirvan falls under the Jalayirid Sultanate (under Kavus I)' 1335-1432 on the Shirvanshah page). Jalayirid page: 'In 1364, Shaykh Uways Jalayir campaigned against the Shirvan Shah Kai-Ka'us' and Kavus 'readily overpowered all of Shirvan and Darband' for Uways; Kavus died 1372/73, Hushang was killed in 1382.

correction.text: the 1344 shape carried through 1385-1404, Ibrahim I as Timur's vassal

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1385-1404, a gap in Cliopatria: the 1344 shape carried forward. 'In 1386, Ibrahim recognized the powerful Turko-Mongol ruler Timur as his suzerain'; Timur 'gave Ibrahim much land' (unnamed) and the region 'from Azerbaijan to Darband' was entrusted to Miran Shah in 1392 (Jalayirid page).

correction.text: the 1415 shape from 1405, with Ganja and Karabakh

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1405-1414: Cliopatria's 1415 shape (47,543 km2, west edge 45.7E) applied from Ibrahim I's independence: 'Timur later died in 1405, fighting and rebellion broke, causing great disruption'; 'Ibrahim used the death of Timur as an opportunity to declare independence and seize Ganja and Karabakh' [quote corrected to the page wording, reviewer eu-19-c, 2026-10-31] and recovered the borders 'as far as Derbent in north and the Mugan plain to the south'.

47,543 km2 (+7.6 percent on 1344): includes Ganja and Karabakh in the west (bbox 45.7E). 1412: Qara Yusuf invaded and Ibrahim, with Georgian help, lost a battle near Chalagan, but the land is still drawn; Ibrahim died in 1417 (infobox 15 September 1417), Khalilullah I reigned 1417-1463.
47,519 km2: unchanged. Farrukh Yassar (1463-1500) and Ya'qub Beg beat Shaykh Haydar near Darband on 9 July 1488.

47,519 km2, but the state ends in 1538 (Cliopatria runs to 1539): 'This ended in 1538 when Shah Tahmasp I dismissed Shahrukh' and Shirvan became a Safavid province. After Jabani (December 1500) the dynasty ruled 'under Safavid suzerainty'; the shape is the nominal Shirvanshah land throughout. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1534..1538 from this entry's own 'valid for 1534-1538 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

region.text: Shirvan around Shamakhi (Yazidiya), the early seat

ledger.note: 861: Haytham ibn Khalid takes the title Shirvanshah. 'The first Yazidi to use the title of Shirvanshah was Yazid's grandson Haytham ibn Khalid in 861'; the Shirvan page has the dynasty ruling 'from 809 A.D. up to 1607 A.D.' (not corroborated, and Shirvan fell in 1538 on the Shirvanshah page). The land is Shirvan around Shamakhi (Yazidiya).

June 1123: David IV invades Shirvan. 'In June 1123, a month after the Seljuk defeat, David IV invaded Shirvan': Georgia took the town of Gulistan. The Seljuk Mahmud II had reached Shamakhi in the spring ('the following spring' after his November 1122 invasion).

region.text: western Shirvan: the piece Cliopatria draws in 1126-1138 (lon 46.8-48.1E), west of Shamakhi, which the pages give to Georgia in 1124

ledger.note: September 1124: western Shirvan is annexed by Georgia. 'Another military campaign was organized in September 1124 in Shirvan': David IV recovered Shamakhi and took the Bigrit citadel; David IV 'annexed the western Shirvan, handing its government over to Mtsignobartukhutsesi Simon' [quote corrected to the page wording, reviewer eu-19-c]. The western piece is read as Cliopatria's 1126 shape.
September 1124: the war ends with eastern Shirvan left to Manuchihr III 'as a Georgian protectorate' (Manuchihr III had been installed by David IV in 1120).

region.text: western Shirvan: the piece Cliopatria draws in 1126-1138 (lon 46.8-48.1E), west of Shamakhi, which the pages give to Georgia in 1124

ledger.note: c. 1130: Demetrius restores the Shirvanshahs in Shirvan. 'This probably happened in 1129 or 1130, when Demetrius restored the Shirvanshahs to power in Shirvan'; Cliopatria draws the full shape from 1139. In 1139 Demetrius raided Ganja in Arran and held it a few years.

c. 1191: the Shirvanshahs' residence moves from Shamakhi to Baku. 'During the rule of Akhsitan I (r. after 1160 - 1197-1203/04), the royal residence was moved from Shamakhi to Baku', the page linking it to Qizil Arslan's seizure of Shamakhi [quote corrected to the page wording, reviewer eu-19-c] (Akhsitan I, after 1160-1197/1203-04; Qizil Arslan's reign is given as 1186-1191); the year is the end of that window.

c. 1201: the Shirvanshahs take Derbent. 'At the start of the 13th century, the Shirvanshahs conquered Darband, seemingly putting an end to its ruling dynasty' [quote corrected to the page wording, reviewer eu-19-c]; the year is the century's start.

1382: the Yazidi line ends and the Darbandid line begins. 'Hushang is killed by his subjects, ending the Yazidi/Kasranid line. Ibrahim I takes the throne, starting the Darbandid line.' Same state, same colour.

1405: Ibrahim I seizes Ganja and Karabakh. 'Timur later died in 1405, fighting and rebellion broke, causing great disruption.' 'Ibrahim used the death of Timur as an opportunity to declare independence and seize Ganja and Karabakh.' [quote corrected to the page wording, reviewer eu-19-c, 2026-10-31] The page does not say who held them; the Timurids are the named suzerain.

December 1500: Ismail I crosses the Kura into Shirvan. 'In December 1500, with the intention to avenge his murdered ancestors, Ismail crossed the Kura River into Shirvan'; he defeated Farrukh Yassar and his 27,000-strong army at Jabani near Shamakhi and 'took Baku'.

c. 1501: Ismail leaves the dynasty on its throne under his suzerainty. 'By this victory, Ismail had toppled the Shirvanshahs' as autonomous rulers, but let the family stay in power 'for some more years, under Safavid suzerainty'; the page gives no date for the settlement, so 1501 is bridging.

1538: Tahmasp I ends the Shirvanshahs. 'This ended in 1538 when Shah Tahmasp I (r. 1524-1576) dismissed' Shahrukh, and Shirvan becomes a Safavid province (the Jabani page: 'the Safavids completely removed the Shirvanshahs from power', governed by appointed officials). Cliopatria carries a Shirvan row to 1539.

wars.name: Rus raid on Shirvan of 1030
wars.outcome: 'In 1030, Manuchihr I was defeated near Baku by invading Rus', who then sacked Baylaqan; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Seljuk invasions of Shirvan (1066-1067)
wars.outcome: Qarategin attacked Shirvan twice, ravaging the areas of Baku and Maskat; Fariburz I paid 70,000 dinars a year, later 40,000: Seljuk suzerainty without annexation.
wars.note: In 1063 the Shaddadid Abu'l-Aswar Shavur had besieged Shamakhi, killing fifty cavalry.

wars.name: Georgian-Seljuk wars

zones.text: western Shirvan: the piece Cliopatria draws in 1126-1138 (lon 46.8-48.1E), west of Shamakhi, which the pages give to Georgia in 1124

wars.outcome: David IV replaced the Shirvanshah with Manuchihr III in 1120, beat the Seljuks and invaded Shirvan in June 1123, annexed western Shirvan in September 1124 and made eastern Shirvan a protectorate; Demetrius restored the Shirvanshahs in 1129 or 1130.
wars.note: The article's war runs 1048 to 1308; this entry is its Shirvan phase. Early 1190s: Georgia reduced Shirvan to a tributary state (Queen Tamar).

wars.name: Jalayirid campaign against Shirvan of 1364
wars.outcome: Uways attacked Shirvan under Kai-Ka'us but a revolt in Baghdad forced him back; he later defeated the Shirvanshah, who stayed loyal to him until his death.

wars.name: Qara Qoyunlu invasion of Shirvan (1412)
wars.outcome: Qara Yusuf raided Shirvan in 1409 (fruitless, especially Shaki) and invaded in 1412; Ibrahim I and his Georgian allies lost a battle near Chalagan, but the land stays Shirvanshah.
wars.note: The battle's year is not given on the page; the 1409 raid is from the Jalayirid page.

wars.name: Battle of Jabani
wars.outcome: Ismail I defeated Farrukh Yassar's 27,000 men near Shamakhi in December 1500 and took Baku; the Shirvanshahs rule on under Safavid suzerainty until 1538.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary or an area for any year; the shapes are Cliopatria's and the Georgian protectorate and vassalages leave most frontiers open. Derbent and the west (Ganja, Karabakh) are the least fixed.

notes:
BUDGET. Nine pages (the budget), one of them (Layzan) wasted on a village. Not opened: any page on the 9th-11th centuries beyond the Shirvanshah article, so the 866-1084 shapes are accepted on the strength of a stable Cliopatria shape and a continuous ruler list; no source for the Rus raids of 913-943 (the Shirvanshah page has only 1030); nothing on the Mongol conquest of Shirvan itself.

STATE. Cliopatria's single row 'Shirvan' 825-1539 is one state, the Shirvanshahs (861-1538), except that its first shape (825-839, 113 k km2) is not Shirvanshah land (verdict wrong) and the Names has gaps 840-865, 1085-1125, 1236-1343 and 1385-1414 that this dossier fills with new keyframes (the first at 861; the others at confidence 1 or 2 because the dynasty is not recorded as interrupted). The row does not need splitting. Pages disagree on the start: 861 (title) against 'from 809' (Shirvan page).

1126-1138. Cliopatria's 5,687 km2 shape lies west of Shamakhi (46.8-48.1E). The Georgian-Seljuk wars page gives western Shirvan to Georgia in 1124 and eastern Shirvan to Manuchihr III; the dossier treats the Cliopatria piece as the annexed west and eastern Shirvan as the 1139 shape without it. If the gazetteer cells show the piece is Shamakhi's own district, reverse this.

VASSALAGES (suzerain dossiers should carry vassal_start/vassal_end with counterpart shirvan): Seljuk tributary 1063-1096 and to 1194 (great-seljuk-empire); Georgian protectorate 1120-1130s and tributary early 1190s (kingdom-of-georgia); Khwarazmian tribute 1225 (khwarezmid-empire); Mongol suzerainty 1206-1368 and Ilkhanate 1256-1335 (ilkhanate); Jalayirids 1335-1432 (jalayirid-sultanate); Timur from 1386 (timurid-empire); Safavids from December 1500 (safavid-dynasty). The Timurid and Safavid rows are in Cliopatria and the me-09/me-10 agents write them.

OVERLAPS. Cliopatria's Georgia row (888-910 etc.) and Kingdom of Georgia (1126-1226) neighbour Shirvan within 25 km; this dossier's only Georgian counterpart events are 1123-1130.

CAPITALS. Baku from 1191 is the page's 'from the time of Akhsitan I'; Shamakhi remained a seat in the 15th century (Ibrahim I died there). Rulers are not given: the page's list was not read in full.

GAZETTEER. Nothing missing: Shirvan, Derbent, Ganca, Karabakh resolve.

UNVERIFIED. Boundaries throughout (no page gives one); Shirvanshah Layzan, Khursan, Quba, Shaki are named as lands but only as the page names them.
